one_line_answer.text: VARK is the most commonly used model of a person's learning style preferences.

cites.quote: VARK is the most commonly used model that attempts to deal with one dimension of the complex blend of preferences that make up a person's learning style.

bangla_explanation: সবাই একভাবে শেখে না; কেউ দেখে, কেউ শুনে, কেউ পড়ে, কেউ করে শেখে।
VARK মানে Visual, Aural, Read/write, Kinaesthetic।
প্রশ্ন হবে 'learner smart কিনা' নয়, বরং 'learner কীভাবে smart'।
তাই ক্লাসে নানা রকম কাজ রাখলে সব style-এর learners শিখতে পারে।

example.en: In a garments class, show a diagram and explain it aloud. Then give a handout and let learners sew.
example.bn: গার্মেন্টস ক্লাসে diagram দেখান, মুখে বলুন, handout দিন, তারপর নিজে সেলাই করতে দিন।

mnemonic.explain_bn: চোখ (V), কান (A), পড়া-লেখা (R), হাত (K): চারটা ইন্দ্রিয়ের পথ।

list_answer.title: VARK learning styles

items.text: Visual (V): information in visual form, such as charts, graphs, flow charts.

cites.quote: learning styles
Visual (V):
This learning preference includes the representation of information in a
visual form i.e charts, graphs, flow charts

items.text: Aural (A): learn by hearing, such as lectures, tutorials, group discussion.

cites.quote: Aural / Auditory (A):
a preference for information to learn through "hearing information".
lectures, tutorials, tapes, group discussion,

items.text: Read / Write (R): learn through reading and writing; text-based input and output.

cites.quote: Read / Write (R):
they like to learn through reading & writing
This preference emphasises text-based input and output

items.text: Kinaesthetic (K): touch things and try things out; they need to do to learn.

cites.quote: Kinaesthetic (K):
Learners with this preference like to touch things (tactile) and try
things out. They need "to do" in order to learn.

traps.text: VARK deals with only one dimension of a person's learning style.

short.modelAnswer:
VARK is the most commonly used learning style model.
1. Visual (V): charts, graphs, flow charts, symbols.
2. Aural (A): learn by hearing: lectures, group discussion.
3. Read / Write (R): reading and writing, text-based.
4. Kinaesthetic (K): touch things and try things out; learn by doing.

keyPoints.text: VARK explores how we take in and give out information whilst learning.

cites.quote: VARK provides a means for exploring our preferences in how we take-in and give-out information whilst learning.

keyPoints.text: Individuals perceive and process information in different ways.
